descriptors.definition: Business encompasses trade, commerce, manufacture, or any trade adventure pursued with a profit motive, whereas profession denotes occupations requiring specialized learning and includes vocations. Profits from both categories are generally taxable under the same head, while differences persist primarily for tax audit and presumptive taxation thresholds.
inclusion: Profits realized in cash or in kind
Single trade ventures if undertaken with profit intent
Vocations included under professional scope
exclusion: Capital receipts generally excluded from business income computations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between continuous commercial operations and isolated trade adventures, and differentiates traditional businesses from learned professions.

descriptors.definition: Income under the business or profession head must be computed using either the cash or mercantile system regularly employed by the assessee. Specific items like certain government subsidies, price escalation claims, and export incentives are statutorily recognized for tax purposes based on receipt or realization certainty.
inclusion: Interest on enhanced compensation taxed upon receipt
Price escalation claims and export incentives taxed upon realization certainty
Government subsidies and cash incentives taxed on receipt basis
exclusion: Accrual-based recognition for items specifically mandated by statute to follow receipt or realization rules
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts regular accounting methods with specific statutory timing rules overriding standard cash or mercantile principles.

descriptors.definition: Profits and gains arising from any business or profession carried on by the assessee during the tax year are chargeable under this head. Rental income generated by an owner from letting out a residential house is specifically taxable under house property income rather than business profits.
inclusion: Active business or professional earnings carried on during the tax year
exclusion: Rental income from letting out residential houses by the owner
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes commercial leasing objectives from residential house property rentals governed by specific statutory classifications.

descriptors.definition: A speculative business involves contracts for purchasing or selling commodities or stocks settled without actual delivery, and must be treated as distinct from any other business. Consequently, speculation losses can only be set off and carried forward against profits derived from speculation businesses.
inclusion: Transactions settled without actual delivery of commodities or scrips
Company share trading deemed as speculation subject to specific exceptions
exclusion: Eligible hedging contracts regarding raw materials, merchandise, or stocks and shares
Forward contracts executed by exchange members
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard commercial trading from speculative transactions lacking actual delivery, enforcing strict segregation of losses.

descriptors.concept_name: Manner Of Computing Profits And Gains Of Business Or Profession [Section 27]
descriptors.definition: Profits and gains are computed following specific statutory provisions covering deductions, allowances, and residuary commercial practices. Assessees can claim expenses related to premises, machinery, plant, or furniture used for business purposes.
inclusion: Insurance premiums for damage risks
Land revenue, local rates, municipal taxes, and rent
Current repairs to premises, machinery, plant, or furniture
exclusion: Repairs in the nature of capital expenditure
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes specific statutory allowances from general commercial expenses permissible under residuary provisions.

descriptors.definition: Deductions are allowed for operational expenses such as insurance, rent, rates, and current repairs incurred on assets used for business or profession. If an asset is used only partly for business purposes, the Assessing Officer restricts the deduction to a fair proportionate amount based on actual usage.
inclusion: Insurance against risk of damage or destruction
Proportionate expenses for assets used partly for business
exclusion: Portion of expenses relating to non-business asset usage
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes fully dedicated business asset expenses from mixed-use asset expenditures requiring proportional disallowance.

descriptors.concept_name: Amounts Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 35]
descriptors.definition: Certain expenditures such as income taxes, foreign taxes eligible for relief, and employer-paid taxes on non-monetary employee perquisites are disallowed as deductions. Furthermore, a specified percentage of sums payable to residents is disallowed if tax deduction at source requirements and subsequent payment timelines are defaulted.
inclusion: Income tax and foreign tax payments eligible for relief
Employer-paid tax on non-monetary employee perquisites
Thirty percent disallowance for resident payments lacking required tax deduction or timely deposit
exclusion: Taxes where statutory relief or exemptions apply without business deduction eligibility
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard deductible operating business expenses from statutory disallowances imposed due to tax compliance failures.

descriptors.concept_name: Expenses Or Payments Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 36]
descriptors.definition: Expenditures resulting from transactions with specified related persons can be restricted if the Assessing Officer determines they are excessive or unreasonable. This assessment considers fair market values, legitimate business needs, and benefits derived by the assessee.
inclusion: Payments made to relatives, directors, partners, or persons with substantial interest
Portion of expenditure deemed excessive relative to fair market value or business needs
exclusion: Reasonable payments conforming to fair market value and legitimate business requirements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes arm's length commercial transactions from related-party dealings subject to reasonableness scrutiny.

descriptors.concept_name: Certain Deductions Allowed On Actual Payment Basis Only [Section 37]
descriptors.definition: Specific statutory liabilities such as taxes, duties, welfare fund contributions, leave encashment, and bonuses are deductible only upon actual payment regardless of accounting methods. However, timely payments made on or before the return filing due date fulfill this condition for the incurred tax year.
inclusion: Taxes, duties, cess, or fees levied under law
Employer contributions to provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds
Bonus, commission, or leave encashment payable to employees
exclusion: Expenses claimable purely on accrual without regard to actual payment mandates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard accrual-based commercial expenses from statutory liabilities requiring actual cash outflow or timely return-filing payment.

descriptors.concept_name: Certain Sums Deemed As Profits And Gains Of Business Or Profession [Section 38]
descriptors.definition: Specific receipts such as the remission or cessation of a previously deducted trading liability are statutorily deemed as business profits. These amounts remain taxable even if the underlying business has ceased to exist or has been transferred to a successor.
inclusion: Unilateral write-offs of trading liabilities in accounts
Benefits or cash obtained from previously allowed losses or expenditures
Tax liability transferred to business successors like amalgamated or resulting companies
exclusion: Receipts unrelated to prior business deductions or allowances
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes normal revenue receipts from recovered deductions or remitted liabilities deemed as taxable business profits.

descriptors.concept_name: Special Provision For Computation Of Cost Of Acquisition Of Certain Assets [Section 40]
descriptors.definition: When assets acquired through specific arrangements like amalgamations, gifts, wills, trusts, or partition are sold as stock-in-trade, their acquisition cost equals the previous owner's cost plus improvement expenses. If such capital assets are converted into stock-in-trade after revaluation, alternative statutory conversion provisions apply instead.
inclusion: Assets acquired via amalgamation, gift, will, irrevocable trust, or HUF partition sold as stock-in-trade
Addition of improvement costs and transfer-related expenditures
exclusion: Assets converted and revalued as capital assets falling under specific conversion rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct stock-in-trade transfers under amalgamation or gifts from general asset conversions subject to revaluation rules.

descriptors.definition: Variations in foreign currency liabilities due to exchange rate fluctuations during asset acquisition payments are adjusted against the actual cost or capital expenditure amount. Separately, general gains or losses from foreign currency transactions are computed in accordance with notified standards.
inclusion: Adjustments to asset costs due to exchange rate variations upon payment
Gains or losses on foreign currency transactions computed via notified standards
exclusion: Liabilities or portions met directly or indirectly by other persons or authorities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes capital asset cost adjustments caused by currency fluctuations from general operating foreign exchange gains and losses.
